messages.content: You are a fluent, native English-speaking member of this community: Reddit, question post.

Readers: Warriors fans on r/WarriorCats. What the writer wants to do: asking readers for their opinions on a plot question.
The writer's note about it, in their words: 我想在 r/WarriorCats 发一个提问帖，问问大家的看法。
A learner's draft:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about the plot that StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he went really miserable and furious for that.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest skies, and it would be hard / not worth it to get back here for a distant little kittypet who want to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it’s natural to be unable to reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when some cat’s at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t go for another try on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
Work in two steps.
Step 1. Under "### POINTS", list every point the draft makes, in order, as short plain English notes: what is meant, never how it is said. Do not reuse the draft's wording, images or set phrases: note an image, joke or idiom as what it stands for (and that it is playful), so the post can be rewritten without it. Include feelings, jokes and questions. Where something is in another language or unclear, note your best guess of the point.
Step 2. Under "### FRESH", close the draft and write the post from your notes alone, as you would write it yourself for these readers: your own sentence shapes, emphasis, idioms and rhythm. Keep every point, the writer's register and tone markers (emoji, "lol", "~"), a similar length, and their order unless another order clearly serves the reader better.
Reply with the two sections only.

result.text:
### POINTS

- The writer is early in *Darktail's Judgment*.
- They're confused about a plot point: StarClan didn't appear when Darkpaw was at the Moonstone, and he became very miserable and angry about it.
- Ravenpaw said StarClan travelled with the Clans and left the forest sky. Reaching them again for a far-off kittypet who wanted to join the Clans would be difficult and not worth the effort.
- The writer notes the book says it was overcast that day. Without moonlight, it makes sense that StarClan couldn't be reached back when the Clans were still in the forest.
- Question for readers: has another book had a similar case where the sky was cloudy when a cat visited the Moonstone?
- Question for readers: can StarClan clear the clouds if they want to communicate?
- Darkpaw didn't try again on a clear day. He chose to transform into Darktail instead (the devil emoji is playful and a little ominous).

### FRESH

Just started Darktail's Judgment and I'm kinda stuck on something lol. Darkpaw goes to the Moonstone and StarClan just doesn't show up, and he is absolutely seething about it. Ravenpaw says StarClan moved on with the Clans and isn't really hanging over the forest anymore, so going all the way back to talk to some random kittypet who wants in probably wasn't worth the trouble. But the book says it was overcast that night, so no moonlight, and honestly it kinda makes sense they couldn't get through. Has there been another time in the series where it was cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or can StarClan just push the clouds away if they really want to talk? 

And Darkpaw never tried again on a clear night. He just decided to become Darktail instead 👿
